_readme: Control-plane config for scripts/find_vendor.py — manufacturer product-literature portals. One entry per vendor: how documents are enumerated (mechanism sitemap|html_index), URL filters, default topic + topic_rules, crawl_delay (build_corpus merges it into HOST_DELAY), and the rights review (tos_url, tos_excerpt, robots, reviewed_at, decision go|no-go). Operator decision 2026-08-30 (see _policy): product literature is ingested as license=open for local training use; declared prohibitions (ToS, robots, AI opt-outs) are recorded but not blockers; logins/paywalls/WAF challenges are never bypassed and Crawl-delay is honoured. Vendors the survey found but has not cleared stay enabled=false with status 'backlog' so the maintainer can pick them up. Tuning loop: after a vendor's first visits, compare pruned vnd-<key> rows (registry/pruned-*.jsonl, reason 'thin' = <2k chars) against kept rows in manifest/vendor-*.jsonl and tighten that vendor's pdf_pattern/exclude_pattern to skip document classes that are one-page sheets.

_policy.rule: Operator decision 2026-08-30 (supersedes 08-28): declared prohibitions — website terms of use, robots.txt Disallow, AI-crawler opt-outs (Content-Signal ai-train=no, ClaudeBot/GPTBot blocks) — are NOT blockers; the corpus is fetched for local training use and never redistributed. What still bounds 'obtainable': never bypass logins, paywalls or WAF/JS challenges; honour Crawl-delay and build_corpus per-host caps so no host is harmed. Record each vendor's declared terms in rights.tos_excerpt for the audit trail.
_policy.superseded_2026-08-28: Freely downloadable = open; robots/ToS/AI-opt-out = no-go (applied to the first 15 pilots; JCI/Trane/Carrier/Taco/Viessmann/Lindab were parked as operator policy calls — now resolved as go).
